planned.title: The seam program
planned.summary: Gives every boundary in the system — service-to-service HTTP, the database, the object store, the metrics stack — one declared way across it, with rules that make silent drift fail loudly and ledgers that measure the conversion until every ad-hoc path is gone.

planned.title: The rule readers are code
planned.summary: Moves eleven thousand lines of non-test code out of this repository's test tree and into a package coverage can measure, so the helpers, readers and analysers every test depends on are themselves unit tested.

planned.title: What a unit owes itself
planned.summary: Gives every unit of code a stated obligation to itself: its branches are exercised, the outcomes it declares are the ones it produces, and the analysers that check everything else are measured code. The second frame beside Plan 180's seams, for what no boundary can see.

planned.title: Archiver endpoint failure contract
planned.summary: The archiver's HTTP endpoints return a summary object instead of raising, so a partially failed job still answers success and pages nobody. Converts each endpoint to a real failure signal, one endpoint per deploy, in ascending order of impact.

completed.title: Testing census and CI restructure
completed.summary: Audited what the automated tests actually check and found whole suites that had never run at all. Fixed those, then built the checks that make the silence impossible: work that skips a test, or quietly stops running one, now fails the build instead of passing it.

completed.title: Distributed tracing
completed.summary: Costed a system for watching requests move between services, then decided against building it: a much cheaper check that reads the project's own configuration files answers the same question, and found 62 undocumented connections between services on its first run.

completed.title: Machine credential lifecycle
completed.summary: Moved the API keys that automated callers use from a configuration file into the database, where each one can expire, be switched off instantly, and show when it was last used — so a credential can be retired without guessing what still depends on it.

completed.title: Commit gate bundling hole
completed.summary: A check that stops this project's public pages changing unread could be sidestepped by a common way of writing a commit, and reported success when it was. Moved the check inside the commit itself, so it now reads what is actually being committed and the shortcut no longer passes.
